He would not have used it in speaking to me. The Mahdi is worse than a hundred crocodiles. Do you understand what I say? The word ‘naughty’ is a good word to use when talking to little children.”

arxiv-1702-04180.title: Traces of surfactants can severely limit the drag reduction of superhydrophobic surfaces
arxiv-1702-04180.creator: François J. Peaudecerf
arxiv-1702-04180.description: Abstract Abstract Superhydrophobic surfaces (SHSs) have the potential to achieve large drag reduction for internal and external flow applications. However, experiments have shown inconsistent results, with many studies reporting significantly reduced performance. Recently, it has been proposed that surfactants, ubiquitous in flow applications, could be responsible, by creating adverse Marangoni stresses. Yet, testing this hypothesis is challenging.

arxiv-2102-05665.title: Non-Gaussian Stochastic Gravitational Waves from Phase Transitions
arxiv-2102-05665.creator: Soubhik Kumar, Raman Sundrum, Yuhsin Tsai
arxiv-2102-05665.description: Abstract Cosmological phase transitions in the primordial universe can produce anisotropic stochastic gravitational wave backgrounds (GWB), similar to the cosmic microwave background (CMB). For adiabatic perturbations, the fluctuations in GWB follow those in the CMB, but if primordial fluctuations carry an isocurvature component, this need no longer be true.

arxiv-2405-16991.title: Concentration and fluctuation phenomena in the localized phase of the pinning model
arxiv-2405-16991.creator: Giambattista Giacomin, Marco Zamparo
arxiv-2405-16991.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Giambattista Giacomin, Marco Zamparo. We focus on the localized phase of pinning models with i.i.d. site disorder on which we assume only that the moment generating function is bounded in a neighborhood of the origin. We develop quantitative correlation functions estimates for local observables that entail quantitative C ∞ C^{\infty} estimates on the free energy density, showing in particular that its regularity class is at least Gevrey-3 in the whole localized phase.

arxiv-2509-16965.title: Preference Distillation via Value based Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2509-16965.creator: Minchan Kwon, Junwon Ko, Kangil Kim, Junmo Kim
arxiv-2509-16965.description: Abstract Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) is a powerful paradigm to align language models with human preferences using pairwise comparisons. However, its binary win-or-loss supervision often proves insufficient for training small models with limited capacity. Prior works attempt to distill information from large teacher models using behavior cloning or KL divergence.

arxiv-2511-22143.title: Stacked Ensemble of Fine-Tuned CNNs for Knee Osteoarthritis Severity Grading
arxiv-2511-22143.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by . Knee Osteoarthritis (KOA) is a musculoskeletal condition that can cause significant limitations and impairments in daily activities, especially among older individuals. To evaluate the severity of KOA, typically, X-ray images of the affected knee are analyzed, and a grade is assigned based on the Kellgren-Lawrence (KL) grading system, which classifies KOA severity into five levels, ranging from 0 to 4. This approach requires a high level of expertise and time and is susceptible to subjective interpretation, thereby introducing potential diagnostic inaccuracies.

arxiv-2601-01665.title: Adversarial Instance Generation and Robust Training for Neural Combinatorial Optimization with Multiple Objectives
arxiv-2601-01665.creator: Wei Liu, Yaoxin Wu, Yingqian Zhang, Thomas Bäck, Yingjie Fan
arxiv-2601-01665.description: Abstract Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) has shown great promise in addressing multi-objective combinatorial optimization problems (MOCOPs). Nevertheless, the robustness of these learning-based solvers has remained insufficiently explored, especially across diverse and complex problem distributions. In this paper, we propose a unified robustness-oriented framework for preference-conditioned DRL solvers for MOCOPs.

pmc-11354013.title: Evolution Process of Fault Silica Aerogel under High Temperatures: A Molecular Dynamics Approach
pmc-11354013.creator: Wenping Yue, Tao Luo, Kaide Liu, Pasquale Del Gaudio
pmc-11354013.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Building fire will seriously threaten human safety. Silica aerogel with low thermal conductivity and thermal stability as fire-retardant material has been widely used in building fireproof structures. However, the natural fragility of silica aerogel will limit its application. In this work, the effects of faults on the thermal stability of silica aerogel are studied by molecular dynamics simulation with large simulation time (20 ns).

pmc-11484329.title: The association between empathy and artistic practice: a cross-sectional study with medical students
pmc-11484329.creator: Martim Fornetti, Miguel Barbosa
pmc-11484329.description: BackgroundEmpathy is essential to medical practice, and efforts to cultivate it often include incorporating liberal arts into medical curricula to promote it. However, the association between empathy and engagement in artistic practice beyond the medical curricula remains unclear. This study aims to assess the association between medical students´ empathy and their engagement in artistic activities.

pmc-11616690.title: Synthesis of defect-rich La2O2CO3 supports for enhanced CO2-to-methanol conversion efficiency
pmc-11616690.creator: Rui Zhang, Xiao Wang, Ke Wang, Huilin Wang, Xudong Sun, Weidong Shi, Shuyan Song, Hongjie Zhang
pmc-11616690.description: Converting CO2 to methanol is crucial for addressing fuel scarcity and mitigating the greenhouse effect. Cu-based catalysts, with their diverse surface states, offer the potential to control reaction pathways and generate reactive H* species. However, a major challenge lies in oxidizing active Cu0 species by water generated during the catalytic process.

pmc-12644827.title: mRNABERT: advancing mRNA sequence design with a universal language model and comprehensive dataset
pmc-12644827.creator: Ying Xiong, Aowen Wang, Yu Kang, Chao Shen, Chang-Yu Hsieh, Tingjun Hou
pmc-12644827.description: Designing effective mRNA sequences for therapeutics remains a formidable challenge. Inspired by successes in protein design, language models (LMs) are now being applied to RNA, but progress is often impeded by the lack of comprehensive training data. Existing models are frequently limited to UTR or CDS regions, restricting their application for complete mRNA sequences.

pmc-12653485.title: Reference Values for Cardiopulmonary Exercise Test in Children—How to Report Them Correctly?
pmc-12653485.creator: Przemysław Kasiak
pmc-12653485.description: Cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) is a gold standard to assess cardiorespiratory fitness (CRF). CRF varied through the lifespan, increasing in children until early adulthood and then gradually declining. Reference values for CPET are used to check whether the child’s CRF falls within the normal range.

pmc-13556914.title: 408. Differential contributions of oxytocin deficiency and astrocytic activation to affective social cognition across illness stages of schizophrenia
pmc-13556914.creator: K K Goh, P-Y Chen, M-L Lu, C Chen, M-H Cheng, C-T Yang, J-Y Chuang, SCAGE Study Group
pmc-13556914.description: BackgroundTheory of mind (ToM), encompassing affective and cognitive components, is a core domain of social cognition that is critically impaired in schizophrenia and strongly associated with functional outcomes. Although oxytocin dysregulation and neuroinflammatory processes have been implicated in social cognitive deficits, it remains unclear whether these biological mechanisms differentially contribute to affective and cognitive ToM impairments across illness stages.
